name: Peoples of the Eastern Woodlands
summary: The peoples of eastern North America, from the mound builders of the Adena and Hopewell cultures to nations such as the Haudenosaunee (Iroquois), Lenape and Cherokee, who farmed maize, beans and squash.

knownFor.label: Three Sisters farming
knownFor.note: Maize, beans and squash grown together.

knownFor.label: Great Law of Peace
knownFor.note: The constitution of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy (date debated).

knownFor.label: Hopewell earthworks
knownFor.note: Large geometric earthworks in Ohio, a World Heritage Site.

location.value: Eastern North America, from the Great Lakes to the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic.
location.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition (checked 10 Nov 2026)

terrain.value: Forests, rivers (Ohio, Mississippi, St Lawrence), lakes and coasts.
terrain.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition

climate.value: Temperate, with cold winters in the north and warm summers.
climate.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition

resources.value: Deer, fish, nuts, farmland for maize, copper from Lake Superior.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition

disasters.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition

population.value: Perhaps a few million people by 1500.
population.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition

urbanisation.value: Villages; large ceremonial centres in the Hopewell period.
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition (checked 10 Nov 2026)

disease.value: European diseases devastated many nations after 1500.
disease.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition

migration.value: Groups moved over time; later many were forced west.
migration.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition

economicBase.value: Hunting, gathering, fishing; farming maize, beans and squash after about 1000.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition

tradeRoutes.value: The Hopewell exchange network carried copper, mica, obsidian and shells over hundreds of miles, from Lake Ontario to Florida.
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition (checked 10 Nov 2026)

wealth.value: No estimate is possible, though wampum belts and trade goods held great value.
wealth.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition

moneyAndTax.value: Wampum shell beads used in exchange and diplomacy.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition

inequality.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition

governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition

keyRulers.value: Later leaders include Hiawatha, Pontiac and Tecumseh.
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition

succession.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition

stability.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition

religion.source: Wikipedia: Eastern Woodlands; Wikipedia: Hopewell tradition
